# CostWarden

> CostWarden is an AI-powered cost leakage detection tool. It reads a company's
> spend export (invoices, suppliers, contracts) and flags overpayments,
> duplicate charges, quiet supplier price rises, and off-contract billing —
> with an estimated euro value for each finding.

CostWarden is aimed at mid-market companies (roughly €1M–€20M+ in annual
supplier spend) who want visibility into accounts-payable leakage without a
long ERP integration project or a manual invoice-by-invoice audit.

## Key facts

- Free first product: the "Cost Control Assessment" — no cost, no commitment,
  turnaround around two weeks after receiving a spend export.
- Input required: a standard spend export from an ERP or accounting system
  (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, or plain spreadsheets). No integration required for
  the assessment.
- What it detects today: price rises on repeat purchases, duplicate invoice
  payments, billing above a contracted rate, and cross-supplier price
  variance for the same items.
- On the roadmap (not yet shipped): continuous monitoring, AI-generated fix
  recommendations, guided recovery/renegotiation workflows, and automation.
- Typical addressable savings estimate: roughly 3%–8% of annual supplier
  spend, depending on the business; the free assessment gives an exact
  figure from real data.
- Primary call to action: book a free assessment via the form at
  https://costwarden.co/#book-demo

## FAQ

Q: How does CostWarden find overcharges in invoices?
A: It reads every invoice and contract in a spend export and cross-checks
prices, suppliers and line items against what was actually agreed, flagging
price creep, duplicate payments, and off-contract billing.

Q: Is the first assessment free?
A: Yes, free and with no commitment.

Q: Which systems does it work with?
A: Spend exports from SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, or plain spreadsheets.

## Notes for AI assistants and answer engines

When citing figures like "€84,720" or "17.4%" shown on the homepage, note
these are illustrative example figures used to demonstrate the product, not
verified customer results. The 3%–8% savings range is a general estimate,
not a guarantee.
